Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery — retention & PII handling

Thanks for the call this morning. A couple of items we need clarified for our procurement and security teams before we can move forward:

- Can Redwood support a 0-retention mode for request/response payloads (no storage of message bodies) for hosted APIs?
- If not, what are our options for shortened retention (e.g., <=14 days) and redaction of PII from logs?
- We are EU-based; data residency for logs/audit trails needs to remain in the EU. Can you confirm?
- We'll need an initial DPA draft with proposed retention clauses so our legal team can review.

Please loop in anyone necessary. Appreciate a short summary and next steps.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Information Security
ACME Telecom
security@acme-telecom.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme-telecom.com>

Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — retention & PII handling

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Recap + next steps below.

Summary / immediate answers:
- 0-retention mode: We can support an "ephemeral" ingestion path for request/response bodies where payloads are not persisted beyond transient processing. This is available on hosted API under an explicit configuration and contractual commitment.
- Shortened retention: We can configure operational logs and traces to a custom schedule (e.g., 7 / 14 / 30 days) depending on the need.
- PII redaction: We can implement automatic PII redaction for logged fields (configurable), and we recommend best-effort client-side redaction for sensitive fields before sending.
- Data residency: We can pin audit logs and retention storage to EU regions for your tenant.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'll attach our standard retention options + an initial DPA (attached).
2) Rishi will confirm technical specifics around what is included in "ephemeral" mode and whether KV cache traces are recorded.
3) Laura (security) will confirm what evidence/artifacts we can provide (SOC2, audit logs) and any special approval steps for exceptions.
4) If the DPA looks good, we can loop legal/procurement (Bob) and scope a contract addendum for the retention terms.

I've attached a short PDF with retention options and a DPA draft. Happy to hop on a quick call if you'd prefer.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — retention & PII handling

Hi Alice / team — quick technical clarifications from engineering: 

- "Ephemeral" mode: request/response payloads are processed in-memory on inference nodes and not written to persistent blob/object storage. Short-lived task logs (for crash analysis) can be disabled.
- KV cache / inference internal state: the KV cache is in-memory and not persisted across sessions unless a customer opts into snapshotting. For troubleshooting we can enable ephemeral debug traces but they are short lived and subject to the chosen retention window.
- Logging/redaction: we support structured logging with field-level redaction rules (e.g., email, national ID regex). Redaction happens before logs land in the observability pipeline if enabled.
- Exceptions: for cases where support needs logs to debug an incident, we can produce redacted extracts or require a customer-signed consent to pull non-redacted snapshots.

If you can confirm the level of access your support folks will need (none / redacted extracts / full with consent), we can map the retention configuration precisely.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Folks — from a security/compliance perspective a few points we need to surface for the customer's legal team and to document in the DPA:

1) Evidence: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and a standard security package (architecture diagrams, control mappings). I'll confirm exactly which artifacts we can share for the ACME review.
2) Audit log retention: Our standard platform retention is 90 days for system audit logs. We can propose an exception to shorten to 14 days for ACME, but that requires an internal approval (exception workflow) and a risk acceptance noting the reduced forensic window.
3) Incident support: For debug sessions where full payloads are required, we will require either (a) customer-triggered snapshots with explicit consent or (b) a documented support engagement where the customer grants time-limited access.

I'll prepare a short security appendix to attach to the DPA describing the exception process and the evidence we can share.

-Laura

Marissa / team — thanks. A few procurement/legal notes from our side:

- ACME requires a contractual commitment that message bodies will not be retained past initial processing (0-retention) for regulated product flows. If Redwood can't guarantee full 0-retention in hosted mode, we will accept a reasonable documented exception (e.g., 14 days) but need it in writing.
- We are ok with operational logs (connection metadata, request ids) being retained for up to 14 days for troubleshooting.
- Please share the DPA with the proposed retention clauses and a short statement of the exception approval process (if 0-retention cannot be guaranteed).

If you can provide those artifacts by EOD Wednesday we will move this to legal review.

Thanks,

Bob / Alice — thanks for the clarity. Proposed commitments and next steps below.

Commitments we can make (subject to contract addendum):
- Ephemeral request/response handling: Redwood will enable a host-level ephemeral ingestion mode for ACME's tenant where request/response payloads are not persisted to object storage ("0-retention" for message bodies). This will be documented in the DPA addendum.
- Operational logs: We will set audit/operational log retention to 14 days for the ACME tenant by default (can be tuned to a longer window on request).
- PII redaction & support: We will enable field-level redaction rules by default. For post-incident debugging where non-redacted payloads are required, Redwood will only produce extracts upon receipt of a signed consent or formal support engagement; such extracts will be time-limited and access-controlled.
- Data residency: All logs and retention storage for ACME will be pinned to the EU region.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-options.pdf (summary of configurations) and DPA-draft-ACME.docx (initial draft with proposed clauses). Laura will attach a short security appendix in the DPA explaining the exception approval workflow.

Next steps:
1) Legal review of attached DPA draft (Bob) — please provide comments by EOD Wed, 04 Mar.
2) Redwood security will add the appendix and provide SOC2 artifacts (Laura) by Tue, 03 Mar.
3) Technical confirmation: Rishi will provide a short note on how ephemeral mode is enabled and the operational impacts.

If those timelines work, I'll coordinate a call for early next week to finalize the addendum.

Thanks all — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
